liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Epic Not Fade Away, with Jerry fanning, Bobby jamming and a powerful drum-driven crescendo; Reviewer names Not Fade Away as one of the show's highlights [13][16]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Standout, poignant Peggy-O, mainly for Jerry's vocal [11]
- **Mama Tried** (1 review): Mama Tried has a polka feel with Bobby, in startling contrast to the Mexicali that follows [11]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Mexicali Blues is played in a calliope-wheel style [11]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer names Minglewood as one of the show's highlights [16]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Reviewer names I Know You Rider as one of the show's highlights [16]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Looks Like Rain is the reviewer's example of the left-heavy mix blurring the layers of playing [14]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet is solid and moves quickly and smoothly into a sweet Franklin's Tower [7]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-12-04.135898.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 179 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd79-12-04.sbd.clugston.2535.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min; rated 3.43/5 by 14 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard quality very good and the solos strong throughout; Reviewer calls this the best sound they ever heard from the band; The mix leans heavily to the left channel, making it hard to separate the layers of music [6][8][14]
- **gd1979-12-04.sbd.clugston.tetzeli.fix-2535.34937.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 161 min [5]
- **gd1979-12-04.frisch.minches.83593.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 176 min [2]

## Around the show

- From the back row of the mezzanine, the reviewer was close enough to see the players' expressions and fingers [8]
- This was the reviewer's first show; the next night at the Uptown was their second, and just as good [8]
- Not the best example of how hot the band was in fall/winter 1979, but still worth hearing [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-12-04.135898.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 source matrix by dusborne;Soundboard (shnid:34937), Master Soundboard Cassette -> Cassette -> DAT -> CD -> EAC -> SHN; Audience (shnid:83593), Recording by… [1]. Also: This is a matrix recording from dusborne, distributed as 16-bit FLAC; Show info is embedded in the FLAC headers; converting to WAV strips the tags, and lossy transcoding should go directly from FLAC [1]
- **gd79-12-04.sbd.clugston.2535.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1979-12-04.sbd.clugston.tetzeli.fix-2535.34937.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Scott Clugston and Bill Tetzeli; source: Master Soundboard Cassette -> Cassette -> DAT [5]. Also: This is the Clugston soundboard source with the tracks made seamless, so it plays without interruptions or overlaps; Resulting SBEs were cleaned up with shntool, and the nonseekable SHN files were converted to FLAC [5][15]
- **gd1979-12-04.frisch.minches.83593.flac16**: taped by Ira Frisch; transferred by David Minches; source: 2 Sennheiser 421s + Sennheiser 441> Nakamichi 550 [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1979-12-04 Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1979-12-04-ticket/) [19]
